environment.timing_scope: canonical replay job execution; fixture generation and initial import excluded

scalar_reference.purpose: benchmark-only reproduction of the former row-by-row compatibility path

non_stable_regression_guards.note: Each final candidate run included the statement-level voice-plaza trigger and the concurrent filter-catalog correctness lock. The current-main baseline and final candidate used the same machine, PostgreSQL version, fixture shape and one-worker execution scope.

voice_plaza_trigger_root_cause_ab.fixture: 1000 rows, 200 existing, no stable account IDs
voice_plaza_trigger_root_cause_ab.note: The trigger-disabled result is diagnostic only; production keeps synchronous projection updates through statement-level transition-table triggers.

correctness_evidence.voice_plaza_visibility: The integration test queries the projection and filter catalog after the ingest transaction commits; both are immediately updated without a background projection job. A two-session regression also verifies that concurrent deletion of the last rows for one filter-catalog key converges to an exact zero count.
correctness_evidence.replay_fallback: The replay integration test rejects any scalar content write and observes stable_author_count=3, batched_remainder_count=3, scalar_fallback_count=0.
correctness_evidence.bounded_sql: The 101-row stable-author integration test requires fewer than 70 application SQL executions and verifies 101 accounts plus 101 alternate IDs.
correctness_evidence.migration: Alembic 20260924_0061 upgrade/downgrade/upgrade and alembic check passed on the dedicated capacity database.

interpretation_limits: These measurements prove the code-path improvement on the controlled fixture; they are not a production SLO.
A 25,819-file production run still depends on file-size distribution, storage throughput, PostgreSQL WAL and lock contention.
The benchmark-only scalar reference is never enabled by normal application configuration or production code paths.
